claim: Rome in June is warm with average highs around 27-29C (mid-80s F) and lows near 16-18C, low-to-moderate humidity making it more tolerable than July/August.
quote: The average high for June is 83 F with an average low of 63 F. In June, Rome averages 30C... and 13.9 hours of sunshine per day.

claim: Late June afternoon temperatures in Rome rise to roughly 29-31C (84-88F) with morning lows of 17-19C.
quote: Late June afternoon temperatures rise to approximately 29-31C (84-88F), with morning lows of 17-19C (63-66F).

claim: The official Roma Pass costs EUR 38 (48h) and EUR 62.90 (72h), includes public transport plus access to 100+ attractions; the 48h pass gives one free museum entry and 72h gives two, with discounts thereafter.
quote: 72-hour pass: EUR 62.90; 48-hour pass: EUR 38.00. The Roma Pass provides access to more than 100 tourist attractions... It also covers public transport and access to the P.Stop toilet network.

claim: The Vatican Museums are NOT covered by the Roma Pass; the pass is worth it mainly if you hit the Colosseum/Forum plus another paid museum and use transit, breaking even after the second museum.
quote: The Vatican Museums are NOT covered by the Roma Pass (they used to be)... you generally break even after your second museum visit and start saving money on all subsequent entries and metro rides.

claim: ATAC fares (2026): single BIT EUR 1.50 valid 100 minutes; Roma 24H EUR 8.50; 48H EUR 15.00; 72H EUR 22.00; weekly CIS EUR 29.00.
quote: BIT: EUR 1.50 for 100 minutes; ROMA 24H: EUR 8.50; ROMA 48H: EUR 15.00; ROMA 72H: EUR 22.00; CIS: EUR 29.00, valid for 7 days.

claim: Rome's transit covers three metro lines (A, B/B1, C), trams and 400+ bus lines; contactless tap-to-pay works on red readers with a daily fare cap (~EUR 8.50) after which you ride free until midnight.
quote: Tap your Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay or Google Pay directly on the red readers... A daily cap of EUR 8.50 applies, after your journeys exceed that amount in a single day, you travel free until midnight.

claim: Rome's historic core is highly walkable, with major sights (Vatican, Pantheon, Trevi, Spanish Steps) typically only 15-20 minutes apart on foot.
quote: each of these sights is only 15-20 minutes away from the last on foot.

claim: The Leonardo Express runs Fiumicino airport to Termini in ~32 minutes every 15 minutes for EUR 17.90.
quote: The Leonardo Express takes you from Fiumicino Airport to Termini station in 32 minutes. The train runs every 15 minutes and costs EUR 17.90.

claim: The official Fiumicino taxi flat fare is EUR 55 to anywhere inside the Aurelian Walls; travelers risk being overcharged (~EUR 90) by drivers running the meter or by higher Comune di Fiumicino taxis (EUR 65).
quote: The Fiumicino taxi flat rate is EUR 55 to anywhere inside the Aurelian Walls... Be careful not to catch a 'Comune di Fiumicino' taxi from the airport, as the fixed fare to the city center is higher (EUR 65).

claim: Pickpocketing hotspots in Rome are the Colosseum, St. Peter's Square, Spanish Steps, Trevi Fountain, crowded metro cars, and notoriously bus route 64; thieves work in pairs using distraction tactics.
quote: Special caution should be exercised at the Colosseum, St. Peter's square, the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain... Bus route n.64 is notorious for being frequently targeted by pickpockets and purse-snatchers.

claim: Common Rome scams include the friendship-bracelet scam, the rose scam targeting couples at restaurants, ticket-machine 'helpers', and unmetered or unlicensed taxis especially around Fiumicino.
quote: The African bracelet scam is the most routine scam in Rome's historic centre... the rose scam, where vendors either lay roses on the table... Taxi scams... unlicensed taxi drivers ripping off tourists, which is especially rife around Roma Fiumicino Airport.

claim: Vatican Museums are open Mon-Sat 8:00-20:00 and closed on Sundays except the last Sunday of each month (9:00-14:00, free), plus fixed religious holidays.
quote: The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except for the last Sunday of each month)... On every last Sunday of the month... the museums are open from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

claim: St. Peter's and Vatican sites enforce a strict dress code requiring covered knees and shoulders for all visitors; shorts, mini-skirts, and bare shoulders are refused at the entrance.
quote: men and women are required to cover their knees and shoulders... The dress code is enforced at the entrance, where guards may deny access to anyone who isn't properly dressed.

claim: Tipping is optional in Rome (rounding up or EUR 1-2 is typical); Lazio law bans the coperto so it may appear as 'pane', and a listed servizio (10-15%) means no further tip is needed.
quote: Tipping is optional throughout Italy... in Lazio... the law prohibits restaurants from charging a coperto. Some get around this by calling it a pane... If servizio (service charge) is listed on the bill, you do not need to tip further.
